global_issues.title: Fed hikes rates for first time since 2023, stocks fall sharply
global_issues.note: Confirmed: Fed raised rates 25bp to 3.75%-4% on 2026-09-16, first hike since 2023, unanimous vote, Chair Warsh hawkish. However Dow's actual close was down ~600-631pts (1.21%, closing 51,461.90), not the 'as much as 750 points' cited — magnitude appears overstated even if plausible as an intraday high.

global_issues.title: Middle East supply risks push oil above $130, inflation pressure rises
global_issues.note: Multiple sources (CNBC, Sunday Guardian, Washington Times, EIA STEO) report oil in the $100-$109 range as of Sept 15-16, 2026, not above $130. The 'Oman crude reached $132' claim is not corroborated by any source found; EIA forecasts Brent averaging ~$90 for 2H26. This figure appears significantly exaggerated.

global_issues.title: US semiconductor tariffs add pressure on chip supply chain
global_issues.note: Confirmed developing: a 25% semiconductor tariff took effect following a Commerce Dept national-security finding, targeting Korean makers with vaguer exemption terms than competitors who secured duty-free deals via domestic investment commitments.

sector_check.note: GOOGL and AMZN as laggards is corroborated by real reporting (Alphabet -2.28%, Amazon -2.00% among session's biggest decliners). CRWD/MSFT as UPTREND leaders is plausible given no contradicting news found; VIX-as-calm-backdrop is odd framing during a rate-hike selloff but not factually wrong.

grok_report.summary: The Fed hike and semiconductor tariff items are accurate and well-sourced, but the oil price claim (Oman crude $132, oil 'above $130') is not corroborated by any source and contradicts multiple reports placing oil at $100-109 — this is the briefing's most material error. The Dow's point-drop is also overstated relative to the confirmed ~600-631 point close. Sector/stock-level calls (GOOGL, AMZN laggards) check out against real market moves that day.
